THE HAPPY PATH IS TWO TAPS.

Tap the tag — or scan, or type — and the record comes up from the device's own copy of last year's inspection. Every check already reads Pass. The tech looks at the harness, sees the record agrees, taps Pass & Next.

The record is read-only by DEFAULT, not permanently: a stray touch cannot rewrite last year's data on a part he is only confirming, but Edit unlocks every field when something has genuinely changed.

The device holds the whole account's catalogue — every tech's items, not just the lead's — so this works with no signal. The app refuses to start a job until it has synced once; without the catalogue every item would look new.

A DEFECTIVE ITEM IS THE ONLY THING THAT COSTS MORE TAPS.

One Fail flips the whole item — the tech never sets the overall result — and the button becomes Add Photo & Remove.

He does not type why. The check he failed IS the reason, and it is carried through automatically; the database composes it from the failed checks and a client cannot override it, so a certificate always matches what actually failed. A photo is required. A note is there if he wants it, and never demanded.

Changed this pass: a New button sits beside Tap / Scan / Type, and on the item list, so a brand-new item never has to be scanned and rejected first.

Also: Edit is a real button on the record; the fail screen asks for a photo, with the reason carried through from the failed check and a note that is optional.

Sample data. Check wording is placeholder — the real set comes from the model's checklist.
